text:
mike: Hey — customer reported function-calling failures when using streaming SSE. They see schema validation errors: \"Unexpected end of JSON input\" from our tool router. Ticket #C-5812.
jess: Can you paste the raw captured stream? Even a truncated snippet helps.
mike: From customer logs (redacted):

```
event: message
data: {\"tool\":\"charge_customer\",\"args\":{\"invoice_id\":\"inv_12345\",\"amount\":1000,\"currency\":\"USD\"

... (stream ended)
```
They reported the final `}` never arrives and our parser throws when trying to json.parse on the incoming chunk.
tara: Do they use any proxy or gateway in front of our API? That can split SSE chunks mid-object if buffering is on.
mike: Yes — request path: client -> nginx edge -> corp-proxy -> us. Customer says they have big payloads in args (nested metadata arrays ~40KB).
jess: Hypothesis: a proxy buffer/chunk-size boundary is cutting the event stream into pieces that our SSE consumer tries to parse as separate JSON blobs. We expect one event.data per JSON value but intermediate chunking can cause a partial JSON char stream to be pushed as an event.
infra-bot: t=2187654338 INFO capture: request-id=req_0x9f3a header=\"transfer-encoding: chunked\" client-ip=203.0.113.7
mike: Repro script I ran locally against our staging with nginx default buffer:

```
# simplified producer
curl -N -H \"Content-Type: text/event-stream\" \
  --data-binary $'data: {"tool":"x","args": {"large": "'$(python -c "print('A'*50000)")'"}\n\n' \
  http://staging.example.local/stream
```
Result: consumer receives two event.data calls, second contains tail starting mid-JSON -> parse fails.
jess: Quick mitigations:
- Ask customer to send smaller arg blobs or encode payload (base64) so each SSE event is atomic.
- On our side, make parser tolerant: accumulate event.data fragments until valid JSON (but careful about DOS vectors).
- Advise proxies to disable buffering for SSE: `proxy_buffering off;` or add `X-Accel-Buffering: no` for nginx.

tara: Long-term: detect partial JSON and attach metadata to logs (request-id + byte-offset). We should also document that function-call args must be self-contained per event when streaming. Add a guard that does not attempt json.parse until we see a closing brace balance heuristic — quick win.
mike: I captured a tcpdump of the connection from the proxy and saw chunk length headers that split inside the JSON:

```
0001: 0x0078 0x0020 0x7b 0x22 0x74 0x6f 0x6f 0x6c 0x22 0x3a 0x22 0x63 0x68 0x61 0x72 0x67
0002: ... 0x22 0x2c 0x22 0x61 0x72 0x67 0x73 0x22 0x3a 0x5b 0x7b 0x22 0x6d 0x65 0x74 0x61
0003: <-- chunk boundary here --> 0x64 0x61 0x22 0x3a 0x22 0x2e 0x2e 0x2e 0x22 0x7d 0x5d 0x7d
```
You can see the JSON object spans the chunk boundary.
jess: Good capture. Can you confirm nginx conf? If it's `proxy_buffering on` with default buffer size 4k, large events will be chunked. Setting `proxy_buffer_size 128k; proxy_buffers 4 256k;` or turning buffering off for that location should stop the mid-object splits.
customer-sre: We tested turning off buffering on the edge proxy and the issue went away for our test payloads. We'll roll this to prod during quiet hours. Thanks.
mike: Action items:
- Support: tell customer temporary fix (proxy buffer off or shrink arg size).
- Eng-runtime: add defensive accumulator for streaming tool args (ticket ENG-1129).
- Docs: note SSE event atomicity and proxy settings (doc PR queued).

jess: Also add a small server-side heuristic: if json.parse throws, keep the fragment for up to 500ms or until subsequent event.data arrives, then retry. Limit total buffer to 1MB to avoid abuse.
tara: I'll create the ENG ticket and tag runtime and security for limits. Mike, can you attach the tcpdump + nginx conf to the support ticket?
mike: Yep attached in ticket. Marking this thread as resolved for support side, but ENG follow-up required. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: incident-log: issue-labeled=streaming-arg-fragmentation escalated-to=engineering ticket=ENG-1129
